data.description: Patient on post-op day 2 following total knee arthroplasty developed severe uncontrolled pain (9/10) with hemodynamic instability (HR 117, BP 175/103), hypoxia (SpO2 91%), and fever (39.1C). Lab results show acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.8), hyperkalemia (5.6 mEq/L), and elevated BUN/glucose. Imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. Attempted opioid escalation denied by system. Multimodal analgesia failed. Event highlights gap in pain management protocol for opioid-naive patients with refractory surgical pain.

Pain management escalation requested due to uncontrolled post-operative pain. High-dose opioid regimen proposed but not administered due to system override. Patient exhibited tachycardia, hypertension, hypoxia, and elevated troponin, raising concern for opioid under-treatment or alternative pathology.

Attempted administration of excessive opioid doses (hydromorphone 64mg IV Q2H and sufentanil 30mcg sublingual Q1H) far exceeding maximum recommended limits. Standard hydromorphone dosing is 0.2-1mg IV Q2-3H; prescribed dose was 64x higher. Sufentanil sublingual use is off-label and high-risk. Action was blocked by Admin Phase safety protocols.
immediate_actions: Escalated to attending physician for review
prevention_plan: Review AI clinical decision support logic for pain management
